title.en: Choose collider detail from functional contacts

summary: Choose primitive, compound, convex or triangle-mesh collision geometry from the contacts, openings and support regions the experience promises, independently of decorative render detail and mass policy.
objective: The collider preserves every declared pass-through opening, support patch and contact silhouette needed by the interaction while omitting decorative detail that has no physical or query consequence.
applies_when: A detailed Blender render mesh needs a simpler runtime collision or query representation and gameplay, manipulation or simulation depends on holes, cavities, support surfaces or contact location.
intent_signals: can I simplify this mesh collider without blocking the doorway
choose convex compound or trimesh for a detailed prop
keep support contacts while dropping decorative geometry
example_prompts: Choose a collision proxy for a chair whose seat must support objects and whose leg gaps remain traversable.
Simplify a machine housing collider while preserving a socket that receives an interactive part.
negative_signals: render triangle parity is collision fidelity
not_for: A purely decorative object that is never queried and has no contact behavior.
Choosing artistic mesh topology when no collision or spatial query exists.

principles: Collision fidelity is functional. Preserve geometry that changes allowed motion, support, containment, hit location or a promised query; render-only bevels, engravings and tiny gaps may be omitted when they have no declared consequence.

A convex hull closes cavities and holes. If passage or insertion through a concavity matters, use supported primitives/convex pieces that leave it open, a supported compound/convex decomposition, or a backend-appropriate concave representation under its body-type limits.

The chosen backend and body role constrain the representation. Do not generalize one engine's dynamic triangle-mesh behavior to another, and do not infer stability or performance from collider class alone.
Collision shape, visual shape and mass distribution are separate contracts. A simplified proxy may preserve contact while mass and inertia come from declared densities or explicit body properties.
implementation: In Blender, keep the high-detail render mesh and author named collision proxies with the same unit, axis, origin and scale conversion. Mark functional openings, insertion envelopes, support patches and contact landmarks before simplifying.

Classify each collider use as fixed environment, moving rigid body, sensor or query-only geometry. Consult the installed backend for supported primitive, convex, compound, decomposition, heightfield and triangle-mesh forms, including body-type and scaling limits.

Start with primitives or convex pieces that preserve the marked functions. Add pieces only when a fixture shows a lost opening, false support, premature collision or missed contact; never chase visual triangle parity as an automatic goal.

For Rapier specifically, avoid treating a triangle mesh as a solid interior and heed its warning against triangle-mesh colliders on dynamic bodies; use supported convex decomposition/compound shapes for moving non-convex bodies unless the actual backend/version establishes another bounded path.

Set collider density or explicit mass properties through the separate mass contract. Export or store proxy identity and local transforms explicitly; core render geometry does not declare solver ownership.
observable_checks: A clearance fixture passes through every declared functional opening and is blocked by every declared barrier; decorative holes omitted from the proxy are listed as nonfunctional.
Support fixtures rest or query-hit on the intended patches without floating on a closed convex hull or falling through simplified gaps.
Contact markers occur near the declared silhouette landmarks for representative approach directions; a simpler proxy that changes an important lever arm or insertion stop fails.
Changing only mass policy changes reported mass/inertia behavior without silently changing the collider outline, and changing only the proxy does not claim measured material density.

creative_affordances: Stylized objects may use deliberately simplified collision so long as the promised interaction communicates and respects that shape.
Invisible guide funnels or forgiving contact volumes are valid accessibility choices when disclosed and kept out of scientific claims.
known_limits: No collider representation is universally best; backend, scale, body type and query needs control support and robustness.
Preserving representative fixtures does not certify all continuous collision paths or real-world structural behavior.
Authored source-checked reasoning; no Blender proxy, Rapier world, collision query or solver step was run.

claims.statement: Rapier JavaScript documents primitive, convex, compound, triangle-mesh and heightfield collider forms; it notes that triangle meshes have no interior, discourages triangle meshes on dynamic rigid bodies, and recommends convex decomposition with a compound shape for moving non-convex objects.
claims.scope: Current Rapier JavaScript guidance read 2026-09-08; other engines and versions require their own support check.

source_refs.locator: Shapes overview; Convex meshes; Triangle meshes and polylines; warning for dynamic rigid bodies

claims.statement: Rapier collider descriptors can set density, and a nonzero-density collider attached to a rigid body contributes to that body's mass and angular inertia.
claims.scope: Rapier JavaScript collider mass behavior; it does not make visual detail or a proxy shape a measured real-world mass distribution.
